title: Hitchhiking Across China: Thumbs Up Season 3 (Part 2/5)
summary: Part Two follows the crew through unidentified roads, villages, Tuoketuo and uncertain Xingye/Yan'an geography. Rides, a rooster encounter, improvised performance and local hospitality sit beside David's repeated sexual, racial, religious and class generalizations. The pivotal narration moves from asking for rides to entering vehicles without permission and remaining after drivers object; that behavior stays literal but never becomes guidance. A private man's tattoo becomes unsupported criminal joking, a building guessed to be a mosque becomes a restaurant, a procession of women becomes nonconsensual sexual material in David's narration, and a claimed police ride becomes a later evasion performance. The final private-home sequence turns a resident and dwelling into Hobbit, sexuality and polygamy jokes whose translated basis is unresolved. Chinese speech, sign content, place names, property access, consent and private identities remain unfilled. Four publisher label categories are exact-span provenance only.
